displayQuote: Every moment is a fresh beginning

meta.title: Who really said "Every moment is a fresh beginning"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: This line is genuinely T.S. Eliot's — Act III of The Cocktail Party, p. 166, where Edward says it while summarising the psychiatrist Reilly. Not a free-floating proverb.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Every moment is a fresh beginning'?
meta.ogDescription: Traced to Act III of T.S. Eliot's The Cocktail Party (Faber, 1950), p. 166 — Edward's words, reporting what the psychiatrist Reilly has been saying. Not a stray inspirational proverb.

answer.label: Written by
answer.sourceLine: The words are Edward Chamberlayne’s, in Act III of Eliot’s verse play The Cocktail Party (first performed 1949, published March 1950) — and in the play Edward is summarising the psychiatrist: “But Sir Henry has been saying, / I think, that every moment is a fresh beginning.” We read it in the Faber and Faber first edition, Act III, p. 166; no rival claimant turns up anywhere in the record.

source.heading: The source

docMeta.dd: 22 August 1949 (Edinburgh Festival) · published 1950, Faber & Faber (UK) / Harcourt, Brace (US)

source.excerpt:
EDWARD: Oh, it isn’t much
That I understand yet! But Sir Henry has been saying,
I think, that every moment is a fresh beginning;
And Julia, that life is only keeping on;
And somehow, the two ideas seem to fit together.
source.cutTag: Act III, p. 166 — the famous line is the clause in the middle
trail: Widely reproduced today as a stand-alone inspirational proverb, stripped of its speaker and dramatic context, e.g. on Goodreads ↗.

Checked against the primary text, not just quote pages: the Faber and Faber first edition (“first published in March mcml” — March 1950), Act III, p. 166, where Edward says “But Sir Henry has been saying, / I think, that every moment is a fresh beginning.” A full scan is free to read at the Internet Archive ↗.

Wikiquote’s dedicated, act-by-act breakdown of The Cocktail Party independently places the line with Edward in Act III — though it prints it as a free-standing sentence, without the reported-speech frame the play gives it: see Wikiquote ↗.

Weakest of the three: another quote compilation lists the line under the play, with no act, speaker, edition or page, and a selection that closely tracks Wikiquote’s — so it corroborates only that the sentence circulates as Eliot’s: see MagicalQuote ↗.
source.excerptNote: The words are Edward’s, but the thought is Reilly’s: Edward is reporting the psychiatrist — “But Sir Henry has been saying, / I think, that every moment is a fresh beginning” — as he works out what he has understood. A page earlier (p. 165) Reilly himself tells Lavinia, “Only by acceptance / Of the past will you alter its meaning.” That is why some summaries credit the line to the psychiatrist rather than to Edward.

author.heading: About T. S. Eliot
author.metaLine: 1888–1965 · American-born British poet, playwright, essayist & Nobel laureate
author.bio: Thomas Stearns Eliot is one of the towering figures of 20th-century English-language literature, known for The Waste Land, Four Quartets, and The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock. He also wrote verse dramas, including the Tony Award-winning The Cocktail Party, and won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1948.
